newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares end higher on post-holiday catch-up.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares end higher on post-holiday catch-up.

text.p: Dutch shares closed higher on Thursday, moving up to reflect Wall Street's gains while the Amsterdam market was closed for Wednesday's national holiday.

"We went up 11 points or so at the opening just because Wall Street was up while we were closed. It was a straight adjustment," said a dealer, adding strong bonds and a rise in the dollar had also given support.

The AEX share index closed 9.40 points higher at 772.74, back from an early session high of 774.56. Dealers said the 775 level could prove to be a near-term resistance level as profit takers step in before an attempt on the 779.02 all-time high.

Dealers said trading volumes were solid but uninspired, with the market lacking impetus from abroad as most of the main European equities markets were closed for May Day celebrations, while London was said preoccupied by voting in the UK election.
"I think we're really waiting for tomorrow when the whole of Europe is open properly again," said another dealer.

He said the market tailed off a little from the opening peaks as investors took the opportunity to bank profits from a rally which has seen the AEX rise around 40 points over the last few weeks. "People have been looking to take profits a bit today, but that's normal after a big rise," he said.
